title: The Chain of Ascent
reflection: On a hard day, ask: which thread can I actually grasp right now? Notice what happens when you take that one, and only that one.

questions.q: A woman tries harder and harder to force herself out of the sense of separation, and finds it only tightens. Which view fits Conversation 5.6?
o: The effort is simply too great, and she tires long before she can succeed.
The split is only an idea, so ideas cannot be pushed against at all.
The walls are too high, and only a teacher can lift a person over them.
Trying is itself a subject straining at an object: one more turn of the split.
questions.e: The split is a subject straining against an object. Trying to escape it makes a subject striving against the object of my unenlightened state: one more split. Pushing harder on the walls is itself another act of what built the prison, so force cannot be the way out.
questions.c: Trying to escape the split is one more turn of the split

questions.q: In the story of the minister in the tower, what does the chain of threads stand for?
o: Four equal tools, any one of which would carry him down on its own.
A chain from the frail, reachable breath up to the rope that can bear him.
A test of his patience, since the minister must wait for each thread in turn.
A way of carrying messages, since the minister is cut off from every other help.
questions.e: The silken thread is the breath, the pack thread the nerve currents and attention, the stout twine the thoughts, and the rope the deep life-energy. The frail, reachable thing, followed faithfully, connects all the way to the thing strong enough to free him.
questions.c: A chain from the reachable breath up to the strong rope

questions.q: An agitated woman is told, “Just be at peace,” and feels worse. Which view fits Conversation 5.6?
o: She is not trying hard enough, and a firmer resolve will bring the peace she wants.
She has been handed the rope; she needs the thread she can reach, such as a slow breath.
She should be left alone until the agitation has passed, since nothing can help yet.
She needs to understand the idea of peace first, and the calm will follow from it.
questions.e: Deep peace is the rope: too high and too strong to seize from the ground. Anyone, in any state, can take a slow breath, and the breath is connected through the nerve currents and mind to the deepest energy. Grasp the thread you can reach, and it leads link by link to the one you cannot.
questions.c: Do not hand someone the rope; start at the thread they can reach

questions.q: A man plans a practice for an agitated evening. Which order fits the chain of Conversation 5.6?
o: Begin with a question about who he is, then rest his attention, and breathe if time is left.
Begin with attention on one point, then breathe slowly, and ask about who he is if he still can.
Breathe slowly until the body settles, then rest attention, and then see any storm of thought as passing.
Begin with whichever feels most natural to him, since the order makes little difference.
questions.e: The breath is the silken thread, attention the pack thread, clear seeing the stout twine. Each link steadies the system enough to grasp the next: breath settles you enough to gather attention, and gathered attention quiets the thoughts. The order is the gift.
questions.c: Breath first, then attention, then clear seeing

questions.q: “The beetle is pushed up the wall by the minister, and in the same way a person must push themselves upward by effort alone.”
questions.e: The beetle is not pushed; it is drawn up by the scent of honey above it. You set the conditions, attach the thread and point upward, and a higher sweetness does the drawing. The contemplative traditions call that grace. The ego cannot climb the tower, because the ego is the tower.
questions.c: The beetle is drawn up, not pushed: effort is the consent

questions.q: A man who gives each day to grasping, reactive action finds that his morning practice keeps failing to hold. How does Conversation 5.6 read this?
o: Action is a rung on the ladder, and he has simply not climbed high enough yet.
The practice is unsuited to him, and he should look for a different kind of practice.
His morning practice is too short, and a longer one will hold through the day.
Offered action is the steady hands on the chain; without it the thread slips.
questions.e: Action as offering is not a fourth rung but the steadiness of the hands that hold the chain. If the day thickens the riverbed faster than the practice lightens it, the silken thread keeps slipping out of reach. Offered action all day keeps the filter light.
questions.c: Offered action is the steady hands, not a link

questions.q: “The four Yogas produce the Self, which is built up over time by action, devotion, knowledge and disciplined attention together.”
questions.e: In Vivekananda’s emblem the four surround the swan, which is the Self. They do not manufacture it; it was never missing. They clear away what hid it, just as the four threads do not create the freedom at the top of the tower but let you climb to what was always your nature.
questions.c: The four Yogas clear away what hides the Self; they do not produce it

questions.q: A scientist on the course wants to test whether the chain is real. Which experiment fits Conversation 5.6?
o: Force himself calm when agitated, then try two minutes of slow breath, and compare.
Meditate for an hour on one day and for none on the next, and compare the two.
Read about the chain for a week, and then rate how well he understands it all.
Ask others if they think the chain is real, and go with what most of them say.
questions.e: Kai’s experiment is to try the two approaches back to back when agitated: grab for the rope by force, then start with the thread and let it lead. He compares which actually works, and reports the result, good or null.
questions.c: Compare forcing calm against starting with breath, head to head

questions.q: What do the four parts of Vivekananda’s emblem of the swan show, according to Conversation 5.6?
o: Four rival religions, of which a person must choose the one that suits them.
Four stages of life, each of which a person leaves behind for the next one.
Four faculties of one person, whose union opens the vision of the Self.
Four kinds of person, each of whom is fitted to only one of the paths.
questions.e: The wavy water is action, the lotus devotion, the rising sun knowledge, and the encircling serpent disciplined attention and awakened energy. Swamiji reads them as four faculties of a whole human being: will, heart, reason and disciplined mind. They are not rival religions, but one ascent.
questions.c: The four are faculties of one whole person; their union opens the vision

questions.q: “The contemplative traditions picture the energy see-sawing between two side channels as holding the split in place, and freedom as the energy gathering in a central channel.”
questions.e: The life-energy normally swings side to side between a cooling inward channel and a warming outward one, and that lateral see-saw holds the sense of me here, world there in place. As the energy gathers into the central channel the wobble falls toward zero, and the ground beneath the split begins to show.
questions.c: Freedom is pictured as the see-saw gathering into the central channel
